    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_21" sourceRef="UserTask_ComplaintMail" targetRef="Gateway_BatchMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_22" sourceRef="SendTask_ReorderFastest" targetRef="Gateway_BatchMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_23" sourceRef="SendTask_ReorderCheapest" targetRef="Gateway_BatchMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_24" sourceRef="Task_ContinueBuilding" targetRef="Gateway_CompleteSplit"/>

rules.instruction: When the description states that an action is performed only when a condition on a quantity or stock level holds (for example, an action is taken only if the available amount is not enough, or only if a level falls below a threshold), and the process otherwise continues without that action: Model an exclusive gateway with a data-based condition placed before the conditional action. Give one outgoing flow that performs the action under the stated condition and one that skips it under the negated condition. Join the two flows with an exclusive merge gateway before the next step. Do not leave the check implicit, and do not make the conditional action unconditional.
rules.situation: the description states that an action is performed only when a condition on a quantity or stock level holds (for example, an action is taken only if the available amount is not enough, or only if a level falls below a threshold), and the process otherwise continues without that action

rules.instruction: When the description states that items arrive in several separate batches at unpredictable times, and work continues until all items have been received, with a completion condition to check after each batch: Model each expected batch as a wait for an arrival using an intermediate catch event, not a task. After each arrival, place an exclusive gateway that asks whether the completion condition holds. Route one branch back to the wait for the next arrival and the other branch onward, so that the check is repeated after every batch.
rules.situation: the description states that items arrive in several separate batches at unpredictable times, and work continues until all items have been received, with a completion condition to check after each batch

rules.instruction: When the description says that one outcome of a choice made by a participant leads to several follow-up actions that are not ordered relative to each other, and all of them must be carried out before the process moves on: Model the choice as an exclusive split with one labelled outgoing flow per outcome. On the branch of the outcome that triggers the follow-up actions, place a parallel gateway that forks them as concurrent branches, and join those branches with a parallel gateway before the next step. Do not chain the unordered follow-up actions in a fixed sequence, and do not join them with an exclusive gateway.
rules.situation: The description says that after a threshold check on a quantity or level, several follow-up actions are carried out for the same item, the description gives no order among them, and all of them must be finished before the process moves on.

rules.instruction: When the description lists several actions that a participant performs in sequence, and some of them come before a parallel split, after a decision, or on a branch that ends the process: Model each stated action as its own task (userTask, manualTask, or serviceTask according to who performs it), placed in the order the description gives and connected by sequence flows. Do not drop a stated action, and do not stand in for it with a start, catch, or end event. A wait for an external occurrence stays an intermediate catch event, but the stated work that checks or handles that occurrence is still a task.
rules.situation: the description says that items arrive from an external source in several separate deliveries at uncertain times, and that a participant starts work on them only after the first delivery arrives
